cleanIntro: The 942 is Taurus's eight-shot rimfire snub, and its book covers four builds - 942 and 942UL in .22 LR, 942M and 942M UL in .22 WMR. Taurus publishes no disassembly for any of them, so this is a cylinder-open clean. One thing to know before you start: rimfire fouling is waxy and heavy, and the 942's eight chambers give it more surface to collect on than any centrefire snub of the same size.

steps.title: Rimfire, and eight chambers - not six
steps.action: Confirm the model and the count. The 942 book's four builds are .22 LR (942, 942UL) and .22 WMR (942M, 942M UL), all eight-shot on a 2 or 3 inch barrel, DA/SA. The operating instructions state eight chambers plainly, and eight is the number to count when you clear it.
steps.prose: Read this against the book's generic safety-systems page, which is boilerplate shared across the Taurus revolver line and says to check that all SIX chambers are empty. On a 942 that sentence is simply the wrong number - the gun has eight, and stopping at six leaves two unchecked. Count the chambers your revolver actually has, every time.
steps.caution: A .22 WMR 942M must never be fed .22 LR and a .22 LR 942 must never be fed .22 WMR. Taurus's rule is that the ammunition must be the same caliber as is marked on the revolver, and the two rimfire cartridges are close enough in appearance to be mixed up on a bench.
steps.quote:
The Taurus 942/942M revolvers have a swing out type cylinder with eight (8) chambers, turning around 
a central axis which allows you to fire eight shots.
steps.cite:
942/942UL
942M/942M UL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev.2 — Operating Instructions, printed p.21 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: Thumb piece forward, cylinder out to the left
steps.action: Muzzle safe and finger off the trigger, push the thumb piece forward with your right thumb and press the cylinder out to the left. Then look into every chamber - all eight.
steps.prose: Forward is the direction; pressing the latch down or in only clamps the cylinder. Rimfire cases are short and sit low in a .22 chamber, so the visual check here is genuinely harder than on a .38 - tip the gun to the light and, if there is any doubt, run a fingertip over the rear face of the cylinder.
steps.quote:
With the thumb of the right hand, push the thumb piece forward. Then press on the cylinder to swing 
it to the left (Fig.1).
steps.cite:
942/942UL
942M/942M UL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev.2 — Operating Instructions, printed p.21 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: Muzzle up, then a sharp push on the extractor rod
steps.action: Raise the muzzle with the cylinder fully out and push sharply on the extractor rod. Confirm that all eight cases have been ejected rather than assuming it.
steps.prose: Rimfire cases are light, thin-walled and prone to sticking after a long session, so the 942 is exactly the revolver on which a gentle push leaves one behind. Muzzle up matters for the same reason it does on a centrefire - a case that only half-lifts drops back in as the star returns - and a stuck .22 case may need a rod from the muzzle rather than more force on the extractor.
steps.quote:
Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure that all fired cartridges are 
ejected. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded (Fig.3).
steps.cite:
942/942UL
942M/942M UL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev.2 — Operating Instructions, printed p.21 (PDF p.11)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: Cylinder out, every chamber looked into and felt
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger, thumb piece depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and the revolver confirmed unloaded by looking into and feeling each chamber.
steps.prose: Eight chambers is eight checks. Work around the cylinder in one direction and finish where you started rather than jumping about, because the failure mode on an eight-shot cylinder is losing your place, not missing an obvious loaded chamber. From here the cylinder stays out - it is the only thing on a 942 that opens.
steps.quote:
Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, 
(3) depress the thumb piece and completely swing out the cylinder, (4) ensure the firearm is completely 
unloaded by looking and feeling each chamber.
steps.cite:
942/942UL
942M/942M UL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev.2 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: A 942 is not the small-frame Taurus it resembles
steps.action: Do not transfer this to another small Taurus revolver on looks. Taurus's own warning is that models which look nearly the same differ widely in design, operation and the location and function of their controls, and they point owners at their site for the correct book.
steps.prose: Inside this very manual there is a live example: the +P ammunition list on the facing pages names the Model 85, 856, 850, 851, 82 and 817 - centrefire .38 revolvers, none of them a 942. It is boilerplate carried into a rimfire book, and reading it as a statement about your gun is exactly the mistake this warning exists to prevent.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
942/942UL
942M/942M UL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev.2 — Ammunition, printed p.19 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: Every 200 rounds - and a .22 reaches that in one afternoon
steps.action: Clean and lubricate at least after every 200 rounds fired, and check for loose screws or pins at the same time, tightening screws and pressing pins in as needed. Then brush and patch the bore and all eight chambers, wipe the exterior, and finish with a lightly oiled cloth.
steps.prose: Two hundred rounds of .22 is less than half a brick, so a plinking session will pass the interval twice over. That matters more on a rimfire than on a centrefire because .22 LR is unjacketed and wax-lubricated: the fouling is soft, it goes everywhere, and it builds a ring at the chamber mouths that makes the eight-case extraction stroke progressively worse.
steps.quote:
The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without any disassembly steps. For 
optimal performance, we recommend you clean and lubricate your firearm at least after every 200 rounds 
fired through the firearm. At the same time check for any loose screws or pins. Tighten the screws and 
press pins in as needed.
steps.cite:
942/942UL
942M/942M UL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev.2 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Field strip complete - the 942 does not come apart
steps.action: Cylinder swung out and eight chambers confirmed empty. That is the whole strip: Taurus publishes no disassembly for the 942, so the sideplate stays on and the cylinder stays on its crane.
steps.prose: There are two exploded views in the back of this book - one for the 942/942M and one for the 942UL/942M UL - and neither carries a procedure; they are parts diagrams for ordering. Anything mechanical goes to a qualified gunsmith, and the book warns that unauthorised parts replacement voids the warranty.
steps.quote: The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without any disassembly steps.
steps.cite:
942/942UL
942M/942M UL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev.2 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

deepAbsentReason: The Taurus 942 book publishes no disassembly. It says outright that the firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without any disassembly steps, recommends a clean at least after every 200 rounds with a check for loose screws and pins, and lists three cleaning tasks - brass brush and solvent through bore and chambers with a dry patch after, a non-abrasive exterior wipe with a small brush for the crevices, and a lightly oiled cloth to finish. The two exploded views at the back (942/942M and 942UL/942M UL) are parts diagrams without a procedure, and everything mechanical is routed to a qualified gunsmith. Nothing deeper is published, so nothing deeper is walked.

cleaning.name: BORE & ALL EIGHT CHAMBERS
tasks: Remove firing residue from the bore and chambers with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent, then a dry cotton patch to lift residue and solvent
Do all eight chambers and keep count - the .22 chamber-mouth ring is what makes the extraction stroke stiffen
Expect soft, waxy fouling rather than hard carbon: it wipes off readily while fresh and turns to varnish if left
Check the bore for light before the revolver is stored

cleaning.name: CYLINDER FACE, STAR & FRAME
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cloth and remove residue from small crevices with a small brush
Take the deposit off the front face of the cylinder - on a rimfire it is greasy rather than crusty and comes off with solvent alone
Push the extractor rod back and clean behind the star; the thin rimfire rims leave debris under it that jams the star proud
Wipe the forcing cone and the barrel/cylinder gap area

cleaning.name: OIL, SCREWS & STORAGE
tasks: Finish with a lightly oiled cloth over the whole revolver for a thin protective film
Keep oil out of the chambers - oil plus rimfire wax is the mixture that gums an extractor
Check the sideplate, yoke and grip screws and press proud pins back in
A revolver with a laser must not be cleaned in a well or ultrasonic machine that submerges it

reassembly: Nothing was removed. Let the extractor rod seat fully before the cylinder goes back into the frame.
Close the cylinder gently until it latches - never snap it shut, which is how a crane goes out of true and an eight-shot cylinder starts to drag.
Rotate the closed cylinder by hand through a full turn and feel all eight stops engage before storing the revolver.
fncheck: With all eight chambers confirmed empty: the cylinder should latch with light thumb pressure and show no side play; hand rotation should feel the stop drop into each of the eight notches; the hammer should hold at full cock and the transfer bar rise only as the trigger goes fully through; and both single and double action should reset positively when the trigger returns all the way forward. Rimfire timing is unforgiving because the firing pin has to strike a rim rather than a centred primer, so if the cylinder does not lock crisply into each notch, stop and have it looked at rather than shooting it.
